name: Knock-Out Whist
description: Trick-taking game where players drop out when they take no tricks. Each round has one fewer card per player (7 down to 1). Trump is turned in the first hand; thereafter the winner of the previous hand chooses trumps. Last player standing wins.

content.text: Trick-taking game where players drop out when they take no tricks. Each round has one fewer card per player (7 down to 1). Trump is turned in the first hand; thereafter the winner of the previous hand chooses trumps. Last player standing wins.

Knock-Out Whist is a simple plain-trick whist variant, often played as a children's game but with enough tactics for adult play, sometimes for small stakes. In Britain it is called Knockout Whist or Trumps; in North America it is also known as Scrounge or Rat.

Dealer deals seven cards each (first hand), clockwise. Uppermost undealt card is turned face up for trump. Subsequent hands: six cards each, then five, four, three, two, one. Winner of previous hand chooses trump after looking at their cards; on a tie, players cut for the right to choose.

items.text: Winner deals and leads: From the second deal onwards, the winner of the previous hand also deals and leads to the first trick. Some play that the dealer leads in the first deal.
Card exchange: After trumps are chosen, each player may discard 1, 2 or 3 cards and receive that many replacements (all at once). When only 2 or 1 card is dealt, only 1 or 2 can be discarded.
No dog's life: Anyone who takes no trick is immediately out; no dog's life hand.
Options when choosing trumps: Winner may choose no trump, aces high or low, and normal or reverse ranking (low card takes).
2 of diamonds: The 2 of diamonds counts as permanent highest trump, above the ace of trumps.
